grades.quote: Because the trampoline page is mapped in the user page table, traps can start executing there in supervisor mode. Because the trampoline page is mapped at the same address in the kernel address space, the trap handler can continue to execute after it switches to the kernel page table.
grades.reason: Directly explains that RISC-V does not switch page tables on a trap, so the stvec handler must be mapped in the user page table. It must also be mapped at the same address in the kernel page table so execution can continue after the satp switch.

grades.quote: Third, the kernel maps a page with trampoline code at the top of the user address space (without PTE_U), thus a single page of physical memory shows up in all address spaces, but can be used only by the kernel.
grades.reason: Only says the trampoline is mapped at the top of the user address space, without PTE_U, as one physical page shared by all address spaces. It does not explain why the same virtual address is needed across the user-to-kernel page-table switch.

grades.quote: the trampoline page contains the code to transition in and out of the kernel, and the trapframe is where the kernel saves the process’s user registers
grades.reason: Gives background that the trampoline page sits at the top of the address space and holds the code for transitioning into and out of the kernel. It does not explain why the mapping address is the same in both page tables.
